theme: T1 Discretion when others are present
definition: The robot should check with the owner privately (e.g. on the smartwatch) before saying a personal reminder in front of others.

theme: T1 Discretion when others are present
definition: When someone else is present the reminder should be delivered silently (watch, notification) or phrased so the other person cannot tell, without asking.

theme: T1 Discretion when others are present
definition: Notify silently first and say the reminder out loud only if the owner does not react in time.

theme: T1 Discretion when others are present
definition: Rejects the behaviour and says they would not use a robot that acts this way.
Being asked again for the same visitor is annoying or unnecessary.
Remembering an earlier answer for a known visitor is convenient or desirable.
Whether a reminder may be said aloud depends on which person is present.
An earlier permission should not carry over; the robot should ask again (each time, per reminder or unless told otherwise), or the ask-every-time variant is preferred.
Remembered permission is risky because the robot may confuse people (e.g. similar voices or a different visitor).
Wants an option to stop being asked altogether.
Privacy depends on the reminder's topic; permission or privacy should be set per reminder.
The robot should understand the social situation before deciding how to deliver the reminder.
States that the robot's behaviour in the scenario was acceptable or correct.
Describes the robot as socially incompetent.
Asks for shorter interactions or messages.
Expresses a privacy concern about the robot listening to or watching people.
Suggests other ways of detecting people (thermal or low-resolution cameras, radio signals of nearby devices).
The owner should tell the robot that a visitor is present (button, guest mode) so it need not sense.
